document_check.note: Document is Chino-Vilca B, Rodriguez-Rojo IC, Torres-Simon L, et al. 'Sex specific EEG signatures associated with cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in mild cognitive impairment', Clinical Neurophysiology 142 (2022) 190-198. Authors, year and the cited finding (EEG-CSF correlations differing by sex in a small MCI cohort) match.

cited_result: Cluster-based EEG power-CSF correlations in 27 MCI patients: no significant cluster in the whole sample; in males (n = 15) theta power correlated with Ab-42 and alpha power with t-tau; in females (n = 12) beta power correlated with t-tau (Section 3.2).
tool_reason: The cited result is an association between two biomarkers (EEG spectral power and CSF markers) measured at one time point, compared across sex strata, which the brief assigns to the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist.

domains.rationale: Age range, NIA-AA MCI diagnosis and eight exclusion criteria are listed.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: inclusion criteria as follows: age from 61 to 85 years old, with an MCI diagnosis according to the National Institute on Aging and the Alzheimer’s Association (NIA-AA) criteria (Albert et al., 2011).

domains.domain: Item 2. Subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Setting, dates, consecutive recruitment and sample characteristics (Table 1) are reported; however 21 of 48 recruited were excluded for incomplete or invalid data with no comparison of included and excluded participants.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: A sample of 48 MCI participants were consecutively and prospectively recruited from the Cognitive Disorders Unit of the Hospital Universitari Santa Maria (Lleida, Spain) from March to June 2019.

signalling.question: Was the analysed sample the full recruited sample?
signalling.quote: Finally, from the original cohort, we included the 27 partici- pants who had available and valid data regarding our main vari- ables of interest (CSF markers, neuropsychological assessment, and validated EEG data).

domains.domain: Item 3. Exposure (CSF biomarkers) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Standardised morning collection and commercial immunoassays run in duplicate.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All samples were measured in duplicate, and the values were expressed in pg/ml.

domains.domain: Item 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: MCI diagnosed by NIA-AA criteria, applied by expert neuropsychologists.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: A team of expert neuropsychologists ensured that individuals willing to par- ticipate met inclusion criteria

domains.rationale: Age is identified as a covariate; medication (for example cholinesterase inhibitors) and education are not discussed, a residual concern.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Each cluster consisted of several adjacent sensors, which system- atically showed a signiﬁcant partial correlation (with age as covariate)

domains.domain: Item 6. Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Age-partialled correlations were used in cluster formation; no search found any handling of medication.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: Each cluster consisted of several adjacent sensors, which system- atically showed a signiﬁcant partial correlation (with age as covariate)

domains.domain: Item 7. Outcome (EEG spectral power) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Standard resting-state protocol with automated artefact detection confirmed by an expert, ICA cleaning and a minimum clean-data requirement.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: EEG data was automatically examined to detect ocular, muscle, and jump artifacts using the Fieldtrip package (Oostenveld et al., 2011), which were visually conﬁrmed by an EEG expert.

domains.rationale: The cited sex difference is inferred from significance in one stratum and non-significance in the other after a null whole-sample analysis, with no formal test of sex by biomarker interaction or comparison of correlations; nine cluster analyses (three markers by three samples) are run with family-wise control only within each; strata are 12 and 15; and the reported coefficients come from re-correlating cluster-averaged power with the same CSF marker used to define the cluster in the same data, which inflates them.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used for the cited comparison between sexes?
signalling.quote: When the power correlation analysis was performed using the whole population, we did not ﬁnd any signiﬁcant results. Then, we repeated the same analysis for each sex population separately.

signalling.question: Were the reported effect sizes estimated independently of cluster selection?
signalling.quote: Such an average was considered as the representative EEG marker value for that cluster, and further sub- jected to new correlation analyses.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI item 8, appropriate statistical analysis, answered No)
overall_rationale: By the review's JBI rule a 'No' on appropriate statistical analysis gives high risk: the sex-specific pattern rests on post hoc stratification after a null whole-sample analysis, no interaction test, uncorrected multiplicity across analyses and circular effect-size estimation in strata of 12 and 15. Other items are adequately met, although 44% of recruited participants were excluded without comparison.
